## Overview

Fill the empty `core/src/agent/builtins/explorer.toml` stub (codex-worktree-relative) with a paraphrased Explore prompt so the built-in `explorer` role finally has a body. The `role.rs` wiring (registry entry + `include_str!` match arm) is already in place — this PR is the **smallest possible delta** from `plans/native-agent-parity.md §2.1`: one TOML file under `builtins/`, plus a tiny test (it must actually parse the TOML, because `include_str!` only embeds bytes — TOML is parsed at runtime), plus a **mandatory same-commit** patch-surface doc note.

The change is license-sensitive (prose is paraphrased from Claude Code's `exploreAgent.ts`, a reverse-engineered reconstruction with no LICENSE file). The plan therefore inserts a **gating operator review step** between paraphrase-and-save and the submodule commit, AND a **separate push-approval gate** between local-tests-green and `git push` to the fork. After both approvals, the submodule commit (with same-commit `// SANDBOX PATCH:` / `# SANDBOX PATCH:` markers + patch-surface.md §14 entry + §15-style rebase-replant note) lands on a topic branch in `gim-home/codex`, then a separate commit on codexu `main` bumps the submodule pointer.

### Technical Constraints
- **`include_str!` is NOT compile-time TOML validation.** It only embeds bytes. TOML is parsed at runtime via `toml::from_str` in `role.rs` (inside `load_role_layer_toml`). Therefore the new test MUST actually parse/apply the built-in TOML to catch malformed content — `cargo build` alone does not.
- **No upstream validation of built-in role TOMLs.** `parse_agent_role_file_contents()` (which enforces non-blank `developer_instructions`) is invoked for **user-loaded** role files, NOT for built-ins loaded via `config_file_contents()` + `toml::from_str` directly in `role.rs`. The plan's new test IS the only guard — by design, since the codex repo prefers per-invariant in-subtree tests (see `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md §14`). The §14 row added in step 6 formalizes this: the test is the enforcement mechanism for the invariant "built-in `explorer.toml` parses and supplies non-blank `developer_instructions` with empty `project_doc_fallback_filenames`."
- Codex submodule remote `origin` already points at `https://github.com/gim-home/codex.git` (fetch + push). No additional remote configuration needed.
- Existing `M codex` in the user's working tree (and `git submodule status` showing `+ed5d2fd…`) means the superproject pointer is **already** ahead of `.gitmodules`. The pre-flight (US-001) stashes this with a labeled stash so the new pointer bump applies atop a known-clean base; restoration/discarding is operator-decided after run-end.
- `codex exec --sandbox read-only` is documented (`codex/docs/workflows/codex-cli-git-bash-diagnostic.md`) as silently failing for read+tool flows. Smoke uses a parent agent calling `spawn_agent` with `agent_type: "explorer"` against a fixed small target (see AC). The plan does NOT set `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` in the TOML for this exact reason — if the role itself locks read-only, the parent→spawn flow may hit the same silent-failure mode. The prose contract is sufficient for this first port.
- Codex's config-merge layer **replaces arrays** (per `codex/CLAUDE.md`), so `project_doc_fallback_filenames = []` DOES override at the role layer. But: `core/src/agents_md.rs` always checks `AGENTS.md` first regardless of fallback list, so the `omitClaudeMd` analog suppresses `CLAUDE.md`-style fallbacks ONLY, not `AGENTS.md`. Documented as a known limitation.
- License: paraphrase prose must be substantive (no verbatim spans > ~5 consecutive words; no brand-name strings in the `developer_instructions` body). Operator review is gating.

### Architecture

- **TOML payload** at cargo-root path `core/src/agent/builtins/explorer.toml`:

    `# Inspired by the design of Claude Code's built-in Explore subagent; prompt prose paraphrased for the codex agent.`
    The header IS allowed to contain "Claude Code" — that's its whole point (provenance). The brand-strip rule applies to the **prompt body only**, never to the attribution header.
  - **Line 2 — `# SANDBOX PATCH:` marker (required by `codex/CLAUDE.md` line 21):** a single comment line per the established `SANDBOX PATCH` convention. Implementer reads `codex/CLAUDE.md` §14 + a recent example of a `# SANDBOX PATCH:` marker in another upstream-canonical TOML/file in the codex tree to mirror the exact format. Suggested wording: `# SANDBOX PATCH: fork-only Explore prompt body — required for the codex `explorer` built-in role; upstream stub is empty.`
  - `model_reasoning_effort = "low"` — matches "fast agent" intent.
  - `developer_instructions = """..."""` — the paraphrased Explore prompt, codex-branded ("the codex agent"), with capability descriptions instead of Claude tool names, preserving the structural READ-ONLY contract.
  - `project_doc_fallback_filenames = []` — `omitClaudeMd: true` analog. Suppresses CLAUDE.md-style fallbacks at role layer. Does NOT suppress `AGENTS.md` (limitation documented in Open Questions).
  - **NOT setting** `sandbox_mode` in this PR — defer until smoke is validated; explicitly out of scope (see Open Questions).
- **Tests** at cargo-root path `core/src/agent/role_tests.rs`:
  - Update existing `apply_empty_explorer_role_preserves_current_model_and_reasoning_effort` (lines 92-105). Rename to reflect new behavior — since explorer.toml now sets `model_reasoning_effort = "low"`, the test should assert: (a) caller's model is **preserved** (explorer.toml has no `model` key), AND (b) `model_reasoning_effort` is **changed to `Low`** by the role layer (NOT inherited). Suggested name: `apply_explorer_role_preserves_current_model_and_sets_reasoning_effort_low`. **Setup note (per Codex review):** seed the caller's model via the same mechanism as the existing test `apply_role_preserves_unspecified_keys` in `role_tests.rs` (CLI overrides or config.toml-driven setup) — directly mutating `config.model` after the layer stack is built will not survive a re-applied layer, so the assertion "model preserved" would be misleading otherwise.
  - Add new test `built_in_explorer_role_parses_and_has_non_blank_developer_instructions` that: (a) calls `config_file_contents(Path::new("explorer.toml"))` and asserts `Some`; (b) parses the resulting `&str` via `toml::from_str::<ConfigToml>` and asserts `Ok`; (c) asserts the parsed `developer_instructions` is `Some` with trimmed length ≥ 200 chars; (d) **for the project_doc_fallback_filenames clearing guarantee:** parse the raw `&str` via `toml::from_str::<toml::Value>` and assert the top-level table has an **explicit** `project_doc_fallback_filenames` key whose value is an empty array. **Use ONLY this raw-TOML assertion.** Earlier plan revisions offered a "seed + apply role + assert cleared" alternative; Codex round-4 verification showed that approach is also a false positive because `apply_role_to_config` rebuilds from `config.config_layer_stack` (see `role.rs:155`), not from a post-build mutation of `config.project_doc_fallback_filenames`. The seed would never reach the rebuild and the assertion could pass even if `explorer.toml` omits the key.
  - Both updated/new test functions get a `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker on their `fn` line (required by `codex/CLAUDE.md` line 21 — `role_tests.rs` is upstream-canonical).
  - **Session-flags layer-count guard (per Copilot review).** Existing infrastructure: `role_tests.rs:586-614` defines `session_flags_layer_count(&config)`; the ignored test at `role_tests.rs:78-89` asserts the count increases when a non-empty role is applied. The plan does NOT un-ignore that test (its hardcoded `gpt-5.4-mini` is wrong), but DOES add a one-line assertion inside our new `built_in_explorer_role_parses_and_has_non_blank_developer_instructions` test (or a sibling test if the function is getting crowded): after applying the role, assert that `session_flags_layer_count(&config)` is exactly one more than before. This guards the "non-empty role adds a layer" regression Copilot flagged.

### Implementation Strategy

The plan **surfaces license risk to the operator BEFORE any commits AND push risk BEFORE any push**:

> **Working directories per step:** All cargo / `just fmt` commands run from the **cargo root** (`<codex-worktree>/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/`). Edits to `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` are at codex-worktree-relative `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` (from the codex worktree root). All `git -C codex …` commands run from the **codexu superproject root**. Each step below names its working directory.

1. **Pre-flight (working dir: codexu superproject root).** **Per Codex round-4 verification:** `git stash push -- codex` does NOT reliably stash an *unstaged* submodule gitlink change (reproduced in a throwaway repo: status stays ` M sm` after stash). The plan therefore uses a **SHA-record-then-checkout** pattern, not a stash:
   ```bash
   # Only run if `git status` reports `modified: codex` (unstaged gitlink change).
   PREFLIGHT_CODEX_SHA=$(git -C codex rev-parse HEAD)           # current submodule HEAD
   SUPERPROJECT_RECORDED_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD:codex)         # SHA the superproject thinks the submodule should be at
   echo "{ \"preflight_codex_sha\": \"$PREFLIGHT_CODEX_SHA\", \"superproject_recorded_sha\": \"$SUPERPROJECT_RECORDED_SHA\" }" \
     > "<job_dir>/preflight-stash.md"   # JSON-in-md is fine; the operator can read both fields
   # Sanity-require the submodule working tree itself is clean (no inner unstaged file edits):
   if [ -n "$(git -C codex status --porcelain)" ]; then
     echo "ABORT: codex submodule has dirty inner working tree; resolve before proceeding." ; exit 1
   fi
   # Snap the main codex submodule checkout back to the superproject-recorded SHA so the working-tree gitlink is clean:
   git -C codex checkout "$SUPERPROJECT_RECORDED_SHA"
   ```
   After this sequence, `git status` in codexu root no longer shows `modified: codex`. The recorded `PREFLIGHT_CODEX_SHA` is preserved in `<job_dir>/preflight-stash.md` so the operator can decide at the end of the run whether to restore it (e.g., as a separate codexu commit, or by checking out that SHA in the codex submodule again) or discard it. **Do NOT use `git stash`** for this — Codex verified it does not work for an unstaged submodule pointer.
2. **Create the codex submodule worktree (working dir: codexu root)** at `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/<job_dir>/codex-worktree/`, branched from `origin/main` (= `gim-home/codex` main) on topic branch `feat/explorer-role-prompt`:
   ```bash
   git -C codex fetch origin main
   git -C codex worktree add -b feat/explorer-role-prompt \
     D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/<job_dir>/codex-worktree origin/main
   ```
   This non-default worktree location is already proven in this repo (precedent: existing `.ralph/jobs/1a-fork-doc/`).
3. **Paraphrase + save** (working dir: cargo root inside the codex worktree). Edit cargo-root-relative path `core/src/agent/builtins/explorer.toml`. Include: (line 1) comment header, (line 2) `# SANDBOX PATCH:` marker, then `model_reasoning_effort = "low"`, `developer_instructions = """..."""`, and `project_doc_fallback_filenames = []`.
4. **Test + format locally** (working dir: cargo root inside the codex worktree), in this order:
   - `cargo check -p codex-core` (fast syntactic + type check).
   - Update existing `role_tests.rs` test (cargo-root-relative `core/src/agent/role_tests.rs`) and add the new invariant test. Add `// SANDBOX PATCH:` markers on each updated/new test's `fn` line.
   - `cargo test -p codex-core explorer` (existing + new tests).
   - `just fmt` (repo-required Rust formatting per `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/AGENTS.md`). Run from the cargo root.
   - Optional confidence step: `cargo check --workspace`.
5. **License paraphrase review (operator gate, GATING).** Surface the final TOML diff side-by-side with `exploreAgent.ts:24-56`. Operator confirms `plans/native-agent-parity.md §4` rules satisfied: no verbatim spans > ~5 consecutive words in `developer_instructions` body; no brand-name strings (`Claude Code`, `Anthropic`, `Anthropic's CLI`) in the body. **Do not proceed without explicit operator approval recorded at `<job_dir>/license-review-approval.md`** (free-text, includes timestamp and operator initials).
6. **Add patch-surface entry** (working dir: codex worktree root). Edit `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`: §14 row (invariant + guard) + §15-style rebase-replant note. **Do not yet `git add`** — staging happens after smoke green to avoid the "edit-while-staged → confused index" loop if smoke fails.
7. **Pre-smoke staging snapshot (working dir: codex worktree root).** Capture `git diff` of all three files (TOML, role_tests, patch-surface.md) into `<job_dir>/pre-commit-diff.patch` so iteration after a smoke failure has a known baseline.
8. **Smoke `codex exec`** against the chosen smoke target (see AC for selection; default candidates `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/scripts/` or `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/docs/workflows/`, each ≤ ~30 files).
   - **Binary identity (critical, per Codex+Claude round-4).** The system-wide `codex` on `$PATH` is the **already-installed** codex which does NOT contain our new TOML. The smoke MUST run a worktree-built binary. **Build command + path are non-obvious in this repo** (per `codex/CLAUDE.md` confusion-points): the package is `codex-cli` but the binary target is `codex-core` (Windows: `codex-core.exe`). `cargo build -p codex-cli --bin codex-core` from the cargo root produces `target/debug/codex-core.exe`. Note this is **not** the user-facing `codex` wrapper — the launcher in `codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot-launcher/` is what users invoke as `codex` and it shells out to `codex-core.exe`. Two acceptable smoke patterns:
     - **(A) Invoke `codex-core.exe` directly** (simpler, bypasses launcher). `cargo build -p codex-cli --bin codex-core` then invoke absolute path `<codex-worktree>/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/target/debug/codex-core.exe exec ...`. This proves the new built-in TOML is loaded from this worktree's `include_str!`. Caveat: Copilot auth via the launcher is bypassed — if `codex exec` requires Copilot tokens at runtime, this path may need an `--api-key` env var or similar. Implementer verifies and documents the exact invocation in `<job_dir>/smoke-transcript.md`.
     - **(B) Build the full stack including the launcher** (slower, closer to user reality). Build both `codex-core` (cargo command above) AND the launcher (`cargo build` in `codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot-launcher/`); use the launcher's `codex.exe` output. Pin the launcher to invoke OUR `codex-core.exe` (env var or config in launcher; implementer reads launcher's source for the discovery mechanism).
   - Record the absolute path of the binary used + the SHA the worktree HEAD is on at the top of `<job_dir>/smoke-transcript.md` (use `git -C <codex-worktree> rev-parse HEAD`). This proves the smoke exercised THIS PR's content. Working dir for the parent invocation: codexu root, against the chosen target as a sub-path. The parent prompt asks for an explorer spawn against the target. Capture the full parent-agent stdout/stderr transcript at `<job_dir>/smoke-transcript.md`.
   - **Pre-smoke spawn verification:** Before evaluating "explorer output" criteria, scan the transcript for spawn failure signals (`unknown agent type`, `role not found`, `failed to load role layer`). If ANY appear, smoke is a **show-stopper failure** (NOT a pass-by-no-evidence). Surface to operator before continuing.
   - **"Explorer output" defined:** the text emitted by the parent `codex exec` session after `spawn_agent(agent_type="explorer", ...)` returns and before the parent session ends — captured in `smoke-transcript.md`. If the parent agent surfaces the spawned explorer's text inline (typical), that's the explorer output. If the parent agent only surfaces a summary, the captured transcript IS the explorer output for AC purposes.
   - **File-path format in output:** AC counts a "specific file path" if it is either (a) an absolute path inside the smoke target tree, OR (b) a path relative to the smoke target dir (e.g., `audit_invariants.sh` for `codex/scripts/audit_invariants.sh`). Generic strings like "the script" or "the workflow doc" do NOT count.
   - **Smoke runs BEFORE commit/stage.** If smoke fails: `git restore --staged .` (no-op if nothing staged) → revise the TOML → re-run from step 4. The pre-commit-diff snapshot from step 7 provides a known baseline.
9. **Stage + commit locally (working dir: codex worktree root).** Once smoke is green: `git add` the three files (cargo-root: `core/src/agent/builtins/explorer.toml`, `core/src/agent/role_tests.rs`; codex-worktree: `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`). Verify `git diff --cached` matches the saved snapshot from step 7 (modulo any TOML revisions during smoke iteration). Then create the commit locally: `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(role): paraphrase Explore prompt into built-in explorer.toml + SANDBOX PATCH markers + patch-surface §17/§14 entries
EOF
)"`. **Do NOT push yet** — push is gated by step 10.
10. **Push-approval gate (operator, GATING).** Surface the just-created local commit (SHA, full diff via `git show HEAD`, commit message) and the smoke transcript. Operator confirms push. **Do not push without explicit operator approval recorded at `<job_dir>/push-approval.md`.**
11. **Push** (working dir: codex worktree root). `git push -u origin feat/explorer-role-prompt`. Verify via `git ls-remote https://github.com/gim-home/codex.git refs/heads/feat/explorer-role-prompt` that the remote SHA matches local HEAD.
12. **Bump the codexu submodule pointer** (working dir: codexu superproject root) — **multi-step, per Codex review.** `git add codex` records whichever SHA the **submodule's main checkout** at `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/` is currently at, NOT the codex-worktree HEAD. Sequence:
    1. `git -C codex fetch origin feat/explorer-role-prompt` (pulls the just-pushed branch into the main codex submodule checkout's refs).
    2. Decide pointer target. Default: the same SHA as the worktree HEAD (the just-pushed topic-branch commit). Operator may instead want the merged-to-main SHA on `gim-home/codex` after a PR merge — that's a follow-up decision, but for the initial pointer bump on this PR's branch, the topic-branch SHA is fine.
    3. `git -C codex checkout <topic-branch-SHA>` (detaches the main codex submodule checkout at the new SHA — typical submodule state). Capture the SHA: `WORKTREE_SHA=$(git -C .ralph/jobs/port-explorer-prompt/codex-worktree rev-parse HEAD)`.
    4. From codexu superproject root: `git add codex && git commit -m "..."`. The commit records `WORKTREE_SHA` because the main codex checkout is now at that SHA.
    5. Verify `git submodule status` shows the new SHA with no `+`/`-` divergence.
    6. Verify `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- codex` (or `git show HEAD -- codex`) records exactly the expected `Subproject commit ...` change.
13. **Cleanup** (working dir: codexu superproject root). Remove the worktree: `git -C codex worktree remove --force D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/<job_dir>/codex-worktree`. Leave the rest of `<job_dir>/` (approval logs, plan, etc.) in place per Ralph convention. Report pre-flight stash ref status to operator for restore/discard.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Filling `core/src/agent/builtins/explorer.toml` with a paraphrased Explore prompt + `model_reasoning_effort = "low"` + `project_doc_fallback_filenames = []`.
- Updating + extending tests in `core/src/agent/role_tests.rs` (one updated test, one new tiny test).
- **Mandatory** same-commit entry in `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`.
- Codex-submodule worktree workflow → topic branch `feat/explorer-role-prompt` → push to `gim-home/codex` (= `origin`) after gated approval.
- Separate commit on codexu `main` bumping the submodule pointer.
- 1-minute manual smoke via `codex exec` + `spawn_agent` against a fixed small target.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to `core/src/agent/role.rs` (already wired).
- Any change to `happy-cli` or `happy-app` (per feature request).
- Porting other built-in roles (`plan`, `verification`, etc.) — separate plan slot.
- New core plumbing for `omitClaudeMd` beyond the chosen TOML analog. If `project_doc_fallback_filenames = []` doesn't fully achieve the desired effect (it suppresses CLAUDE.md-style fallbacks but not `AGENTS.md`), plan defers the gap.
- Setting `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` — explicitly deferred to a follow-up PR after this one's smoke is proven, because of the documented `codex exec --sandbox read-only` silent-failure mode.
- Un-ignoring `apply_explorer_role_sets_model_and_adds_session_flags_layer` (lines 78-89 in role_tests.rs) — its hardcoded `gpt-5.4-mini` expectation is unrelated.

## Risk Areas

1. **License compliance (HIGH, gating).** Paraphrased prose must satisfy `plans/native-agent-parity.md §4`. Mitigation: explicit operator-review step (#5) BEFORE any commits, approval artifact `<job_dir>/license-review-approval.md`.
2. **Premature push to fork (HIGH, gating).** Mitigation: explicit push-approval gate (#10) AFTER smoke green, approval artifact `<job_dir>/push-approval.md`.
3. **Missing SANDBOX PATCH markers / patch-surface entries breaking fork discipline (HIGH → mitigated).** `codex/CLAUDE.md` line 21 mandates `// SANDBOX PATCH:` / `# SANDBOX PATCH:` markers on every edited line of upstream-canonical files + a §14 row + a §15-style rebase-replant note. Mitigation: markers required on TOML line 2 AND each updated/new test `fn` line (AC); §14 + §15 entries required in step #6 same-commit.
4. **Submodule pointer ordering (MODERATE).** If we bump the codexu pointer before the fork push completes, fresh clones break. Mitigation: explicit ordering #11 (push first) → #12 (bump pointer), with `git ls-remote` verification in #11.
5. **Pre-existing `M codex` pointer (MODERATE).** User's working tree already has an unstaged submodule pointer change; ignoring it would either lose that change or accidentally roll it into our pointer-bump commit. Mitigation: pre-flight step #1 uses a **path-scoped** stash (`git stash push -m ... -- codex`, NO `-u`) to isolate just the gitlink without disturbing `.worktrees/`, `tasks/`, `packages/happy-app/` etc.
6. **Smoke iteration leaving confused index (MODERATE → mitigated).** If smoke fails after files are staged, the operator would be confused about what's staged vs working-tree. Mitigation: step #6 explicitly defers `git add` until after smoke (#8); step #7 captures a `pre-commit-diff.patch` snapshot for iteration baseline.
7. **Test rename misnaming behavior (LOW → mitigated).** The renamed test asserts `model_reasoning_effort` is CHANGED to `Low` (not "inherited") since explorer.toml now sets it. Mitigation: name and assertion spelled out in Architecture and AC.
8. **`include_str!` does not validate TOML at compile time (LOW → mitigated).** Mitigation: new test explicitly parses the embedded TOML via `toml::from_str`.
9. **Smoke flow gotchas (LOW).** `codex exec --sandbox read-only` known-broken; we use parent + `spawn_agent` and we deliberately do NOT set `sandbox_mode = "read-only"` in the TOML.
10. **`AGENTS.md` still loads (LOW, documented).** `project_doc_fallback_filenames = []` doesn't suppress `AGENTS.md`. Documented in Open Questions for operator review.
11. **Worktree path under `.ralph/jobs/`.** Non-standard location for a git worktree (typical is `.worktrees/`). Mitigation: precedent exists in this repo (`.ralph/jobs/1a-fork-doc/`); cleanup in step #13.

(The header is required by `plans/native-agent-parity.md §4` to identify the inspiration; the SANDBOX PATCH marker is required by `codex/CLAUDE.md` line 21; both are explicitly exempt from this rule.)
- [ ] No verbatim span of > 5 consecutive words from `exploreAgent.ts:24-56` appears in `explorer.toml`'s `developer_instructions` body. Verified by operator side-by-side review; approval recorded at `<job_dir>/license-review-approval.md` BEFORE the submodule commit.
- [ ] Each updated/new test function in `core/src/agent/role_tests.rs` carries a `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker on its `fn` line.
- [ ] `cargo check -p codex-core` succeeds from `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/` inside the codex worktree.
- [ ] `cargo test -p codex-core explorer` passes (updated existing test + new invariant test).
- [ ] The new test `built_in_explorer_role_parses_and_has_non_blank_developer_instructions` does ALL of: (a) calls `config_file_contents(Path::new("explorer.toml"))` and asserts `Some(...)`; (b) parses the returned `&str` via `toml::from_str::<ConfigToml>` and asserts `Ok`; (c) asserts the parsed `developer_instructions` is `Some` with trimmed length ≥ 200; (d) **strong project_doc_fallback_filenames clearing assertion — raw-TOML form only**: parse the raw `&str` via `toml::from_str::<toml::Value>` and assert the top-level table has an **explicit** key `project_doc_fallback_filenames` with an empty-array value. Codex round-4 verified that both the `ConfigToml`-default check and the seed-then-apply-role alternative are false positives.
- [ ] The renamed existing test asserts both (a) caller's `model` is preserved AND (b) `model_reasoning_effort` is set to `Low` by the role layer (i.e., the role CHANGES it, does not inherit caller's). Setup seeds the caller's model via CLI overrides or config.toml (like `apply_role_preserves_unspecified_keys`), NOT by mutating `config.model` directly after the layer stack is built.
- [ ] A test asserts the explorer role **adds one session-flags layer** (using existing `session_flags_layer_count(&config)` helper in `role_tests.rs:586-614`): count before vs after `apply_role_to_config(&mut config, Some("explorer"))` differs by exactly 1. This guards against silent "role applies but layer is empty" regressions.
- [ ] `just fmt` is run from `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/` after Rust edits; `git status` shows no formatting drift.
- [ ] `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` gains BOTH (a) a new top-level section (likely §17 "Built-in agent role: `explorer` prompt") with prose summary + file-role table + "Important invariants" list, AND (b) a new row in §14's invariant-to-test mapping table (row **21** — verified: §14 has rows 1–20 already) referencing the new test by path: `core/src/agent/role_tests.rs::built_in_explorer_role_parses_and_has_non_blank_developer_instructions`. The new §17 includes per-section rebase guidance. **Both edits land in the same commit as the TOML and test edits.**
- [ ] License-paraphrase review approval recorded at `<job_dir>/license-review-approval.md` before any submodule commit.
- [ ] Pre-commit diff snapshot saved to `<job_dir>/pre-commit-diff.patch` before smoke.
- [ ] **Smoke target chosen and recorded at the top of `<job_dir>/smoke-transcript.md`.** Plan default: `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/scripts/` (codex repo scripts dir) OR `D:/harness-efforts/codexu/codex/docs/workflows/` — both are ≤ ~30 files. Operator picks one of these or another ≤ ~30-file target before smoke runs. Recording the choice IS the gate; the prior recommendation of `packages/codium/` is RESCINDED (that dir has ~1650 files).
- [ ] **Binary identity recorded** at the top of `<job_dir>/smoke-transcript.md`: absolute path of the `codex` binary used MUST be a worktree-built `target/debug/codex(.exe)` or `target/release/codex(.exe)` — NOT a `$PATH`-resolved system codex. Also record `git -C <codex-worktree> rev-parse HEAD` to prove smoke exercised this PR's content.
- [ ] Smoke pass criteria (recorded in `<job_dir>/smoke-transcript.md`): (a) explorer output names ≥ 2 specific file paths from the target. (b) transcript shows zero write/edit/modification activity. Scope the check to **structured tool-call entries only** (NOT free prose anywhere in the transcript — Codex round-4 flagged that raw-text scans false-positive on the model naturally mentioning words like `Write` or `>` in commentary). The two-pass scan: (i) for each tool-call entry (e.g., a JSON object or labeled block with a `tool` / `function_call` field), if the tool name is one of `Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `apply_patch`, `NotebookEdit`, fail. (ii) for each shell/bash tool-call entry, examine its `command` argument only; if it contains a redirect operator (`>`, `>>`), a heredoc (`<<`), or invokes `mkdir`, `rm`, `rmdir`, `touch`, `mv`, `cp`, `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git reset`, `python -c`, `python3 -c`, `powershell ... Set-Content`/`Out-File`/`Add-Content`, `node -e`, `sed -i`, `awk ... > ...`, or `tee`, fail. If the transcript format does not separate tool calls from prose (worst case), narrow the scan to the agent's own tool-call output blocks rather than the entire stdout.
- [ ] Push-approval recorded at `<job_dir>/push-approval.md` before `git push`.
- [ ] Topic branch `feat/explorer-role-prompt` pushed to `origin` (= `gim-home/codex`); reachable via `git ls-remote https://github.com/gim-home/codex.git refs/heads/feat/explorer-role-prompt`.
- [ ] Separate commit on codexu `main` bumps the submodule pointer; `git submodule status` shows the new SHA with no `+`/`-` divergence.
- [ ] Codex submodule worktree under `.ralph/jobs/<job_dir>/codex-worktree/` is removed at end of run; pre-flight stash ref reported in `<job_dir>/preflight-stash.md` (restore/discard pending operator decision).
